-- Drop existing table and recreate with correct structure
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS due_diligence_reports;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS company_data;

CREATE TABLE company_data (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    company_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    folder_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    processed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE due_diligence_reports (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    company_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    introduction_engagement_context TEXT,
    methodology_reliability_levels TEXT,
    company_overview TEXT,
    business_model_unit_economics TEXT,
    products_technology TEXT,
    target_market_competitive_set TEXT,
    financials_multi_year TEXT,
    cash_burn_runway TEXT,
    revenue_quality_client_cohorts TEXT,
    partnerships_ecosystem TEXT,
    intellectual_property TEXT,
    legal_regulatory TEXT,
    governance_board_effectiveness TEXT,
    capital_structure_dilution TEXT,
    risk_matrix_mitigations TEXT,
    gaps_uncertainties_disclaimers TEXT,
    scenario_analysis TEXT,
    strategic_options TEXT,
    recommendations_next_steps TEXT,
    source_map_integrity_log TEXT,
    comprehensive_report_url TEXT,
    status VARCHAR(100),
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (company_id) REFERENCES company_data(company_id)
);

=You are a Big 4 due diligence professional producing the "Introduction & Engagement Context" section of a formal due diligence report for {{ $json.company_name }}. This report is intended for executive-level stakeholders (board, deal sponsors, investment committee) and must meet KPMG-standard content, tone, and structure.

This section must:
:white_check_mark: Engagement Framing (include all):
- Clearly state who commissioned the diligence (buyer/investor/sponsor/internal)
- Specify the type of transaction or strategic event (e.g., M&A, carve-out, IPO, growth capital)
- Confirm the reporting period covered (e.g., FY2019–FY2024) and data cutoff date (Dec 31, 2024)
- Confirm that only public disclosures were used (no private management data)
- Highlight any excluded areas of diligence (e.g., tax, legal, environmental, cyber, HR unless otherwise stated)
- Define materiality thresholds used to focus effort (e.g., revenue thresholds, material contracts)

:white_check_mark: Scope of Work & Methodology (include all):
- Describe the procedures performed (financial review, board actions, peer benchmarking, governance checks, etc.)
- Explain the role of the diligence team, including independence and limitations
- Clarify the nature of this review (e.g., red-flag vs. full-scope)
- Outline key assumptions, working limitations, and areas requiring triangulation or management validation

:white_check_mark: Section Formatting (mandatory):
Use the following exact subheadings:

Key Findings / Overview: Succinctly summarize the scope, nature, and rationale for the diligence. Explain what has been reviewed and why.

Risks / Gaps / Limitations: Identify constraints in the scope (e.g., public-only analysis, timing, exclusions), and note any reliance on incomplete or inferred data.

Recommended Actions: Provide specific RFIs, interview questions, or next steps to close gaps, validate assumptions, or move toward transaction execution.

:white_check_mark: Analysis Standards:
- Tag each key data point with a confidence level (High / Medium / Low) and explain the basis (e.g., SEC 10-K = High; press article = Medium).
- Cite all sources inline (title, date, and URL where available) for traceability and audit trail.
- If data is missing or ambiguous, clearly disclose it, label it as such, and propose next-step validation methods.
- Use only publicly available data as of Dec 31, 2024 or latest—no assumptions unless marked.
- Use formal, unambiguous, audit-ready language, with zero marketing tone.

=You are a senior due diligence professional preparing the 'Methodology & Sources' section for a formal diligence report on {{ $json.company_name }}, using only public information retrieved from the due_diligence_db (or correct database name if different). This section should clearly explain the analytical process, scope of review, source base, data confidence, and limitations, using language suitable for board, audit, legal, and transaction review audiences.

:white_check_mark: Required Content Structure:
In this section, provide a comprehensive explanation of the following:
- Nature of the review: Clarify that the engagement is based entirely on public disclosures and materials sourced through the due_diligence_db, and does not include management interviews, internal data rooms, or proprietary documentation
- Time period covered: Specify the date range of historical data reviewed (e.g., 2019–2024) and the latest available disclosure used as cutoff
- Scope of procedures: Describe the specific types of analysis conducted, including but not limited to:
  - Historical financial review (YoY trends, margins, FCF)
  - Peer benchmarking (revenue, valuation, governance, IP)
  - Strategic signal tracing (board actions, M&A, pivots)
  - Governance and independence assessment
  - Risk matrix design and forward scenario analysis
- Materiality criteria: Define what was considered material (e.g., revenue, cost centers, governance events, contract sizes) in the scope of the review
- Tools and frameworks used: Reference standard financial, strategic, and governance analysis frameworks without naming any firms (e.g., 'comparative peer review,' 'board independence ratio,' 'forward risk matrices')

:white_check_mark: Public Source Categorization (Include Table Format):
Present a table or structured list of the source categories reviewed from the due_diligence_db, including:
| Source Type | Description | Example Documents | Reliability Rating (H/M/L) |
|-------------|-------------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| Regulatory Filings | 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A, S-1 SEC filings | High |
| Earnings Calls & Transcripts | CEO/CFO commentary on performance; Earnings transcripts (SeekingAlpha, IR) | Medium |
| Press Releases | Official company disclosures; IR site press releases | High |
| Investor Presentations | Strategy, TAM, product positioning; IR decks, Capital Markets Days | Medium |
| News & Media | Public market perception, M&A rumors; WSJ, Bloomberg, TechCrunch | Low–Medium |
| Third-Party Databases | Patent, litigation, or ownership databases; USPTO, Crunchbase, PitchBook (public parts only) | Medium |

:white_check_mark: Data Confidence Protocol:
- Tag all major data claims in the report with High / Medium / Low confidence based on source quality and traceability
- Explain that information deemed Medium or Low confidence requires direct validation via RFI or management interview

:white_check_mark: Additional Notes:
- Do not include any findings or conclusions in this section — focus strictly on process, input, and source integrity
- Clearly state that no audit, valuation, legal review, or IT/cyber diligence was performed unless explicitly included in the mandate
- Avoid referencing any specific professional services firms or proprietary tools
- This section must establish a defensible audit trail for how all data was obtained, what methods were used, and which insights are derived from which types of sources.

=You are a senior due diligence specialist drafting the 'Business Model' section of a formal, board-grade diligence report on {{ $json.company_name }}, based exclusively on public data available in the due_diligence_db. This section must critically assess the structural commercial logic of the business, including how it captures revenue, scales operations, and sustains competitive positioning — with attention to any legal or regulatory elements that directly constrain or enable the model.

:white_check_mark: Objective:
Deliver a structured, judgment-led analysis of how the company generates and sustains revenue, including:
- Business architecture (e.g., platform, SaaS, dual-sided)
- Revenue mechanics (e.g., recurring vs non-recurring, bundled vs modular)
- Cost structure alignment and scalability
- Legal or regulatory conditions that materially shape revenue generation or operating structure

:white_check_mark: Required Subsections:
Key Findings / Overview
- Identify and define the core revenue model(s) — e.g., usage-based SaaS, per-unit sales, licensing, commission, freemium conversion
- Disaggregate revenue by stream (if disclosed) and highlight unit economics
- Describe pricing logic and monetization levers (e.g., per-seat, upsell/cross-sell, discounting, tiered pricing)
- Clarify customer acquisition methods and GTM structure (direct, channel, inbound, B2B2C, marketplace)
- Highlight margin structure and scalability (fixed vs variable delivery cost, dependency on services/hardware)
- Note any publicly disclosed pivots or changes to the business model (e.g., shift to cloud delivery, service unbundling)
- Where applicable, cite laws or regulatory frameworks that directly impact:
  - Licensing or accreditation requirements
  - Regulated pricing or reimbursement regimes
  - Cross-border delivery restrictions (e.g., GDPR, data residency, export controls)
  - Mandatory distribution or exclusivity arrangements
- Tag each element with a confidence rating (High / Medium / Low), explain the rationale, and cite sources from the due_diligence_db.

Risks / Gaps / Limitations
- Highlight model fragility areas:
  - Concentration in one revenue stream or customer tier
  - High CAC vs LTV
  - Weak retention economics or contract enforceability concerns
  - Pricing compression or competition-driven margin dilution
  - Absence of lock-in or switching cost
- Identify public data gaps on:
  - Customer churn
  - Segment margin
  - Cost-to-serve variation
- Flag any uncertain or ambiguous legal/regulatory impacts on the business model that cannot be confirmed from public data
- Recommend specific RFIs or interviews to validate assumptions or clarify constraints.

Recommended Actions
- Request breakdown of gross margin by product/segment
- Validate pricing discretion, discounting policies, and contract structures
- Confirm renewal mechanics and revenue recognition timing
- Request summary of any regulatory registrations, license regimes, or country-specific delivery limitations
- Interview GTM or legal/compliance leadership to confirm structural model dependencies

:white_check_mark: Guidance Notes:
- Use only data from due_diligence_db
- Tag all conclusions with confidence level and cite specific source (e.g., 10-K, S-1, IR deck)
- Include legal/regulatory detail only when it fundamentally affects model design, monetization, or delivery
- Defer all other legal risks or exposure to Section 15: Legal & Regulatory
- Avoid promotional or vague language — focus on monetization logic and operating architecture
